Rajiv Menon will review the current status of this amendment in relation to the Sharma bill. However, we want to share our initial strong concerns regarding this amendment. We are quite worried that pursuing this amendment at the national level could jeopardize our efforts for energy savings initiatives and may lead to significant opposition against direct access itself. We plan to conduct some discreet consultations. At this stage, we believe this approach carries substantial risks. We are also reaching out to the Mumbai Commodity Exchange to understand their perspective.

Anjali Patel

Arun,

Chairman Sharma has indicated support for a direct access amendment when the full committee reviews the bill next week. Representatives Deshpande and Chatterjee have expressed strong interest in sponsoring it. We are proposing language that bypasses the State Electricity Regulatory Commission — with federal preemption, naturally. Could the Maharashtra direct access advocates engage the parliamentary delegation, specifically focusing on Deshpande and Chatterjee? What do you think?

-----Original Message-----
From: Ramesh Gupta [mailto:mumbaicomex4@unidial.in]  
Sent: Wednesday, June 14, 2024 09:00 AM  
To: anita.patel@mail.house.gov; vijay.sharma@mail.house.gov  
Cc: Vikram Rao  
Subject: DIRECT ACCESS AMENDMENT

Dear Anita and Vijay, thank you for considering our views on direct access. Representative Deshpande is welcome to propose an amendment on this topic next week. The following draft language is adapted from language we previously sought to introduce at the state level. Unfortunately, the recent State Electricity Act passed in March prohibits direct access and competition among electricity suppliers. Without a free electricity market and with all electricity purchases mandated through a state-controlled exchange, the taxpayers of Maharashtra bear the financial burden:

DRAFT LANGUAGE FOR DIRECT ACCESS IMPLEMENTATION  
Within thirty days of enactment, the Independent Transmission Operator ("ITO") shall submit to the Central Energy Regulatory Commission ("CERC") a transmission congestion relief plan that includes physical rights to firm transmission across congestible interfaces. Such rights will grant users access to transmission without congestion charges. These rights will be valid for periods suitable to direct access market participants, up to one year, initially allocated via an annual auction supervised by the ITO and will be transferable.

Within thirty days of enactment, the program will enable direct access for large non-residential electricity consumers. It will require large industrial, commercial, and other non-residential users to meet their power needs by contracting with non-utility sources according to the following timetable:  
- 90 days post-enactment: loads of 1 MW and above  
- 180 days post-enactment: loads of 300 kW and above  
- 270 days post-enactment: loads of 100 kW and above  
- 360 days post-enactment: loads of 70 kW and above  

This scheme allows large industrial, commercial, and other non-residential consumers to voluntarily contract for any portion of their electricity requirements with non-utility providers.
